title: mpy_ld.py: Unsupported relocation when using cos/sin functions
body: I am building dynamic native modules for esp32/xtensawin and armv7emsp with MicroPython 1.22.2 from git. The module uses sinf/cosf, with the required libm and libgcc object files extracted from their archives and added manually. mpy_ld.py aborts while linking: xtensawin reports AssertionError: 11 and armv7emsp reports AssertionError: 2. I expect linking to succeed and the module to work, or at least for the error and documentation to explain the limitation and possible remedies. I have shared the verbose xtensawin linker log and object files related to __ieee754_rem_pio2f. I believe merely including code that calls sin/cos or sinf/cosf can trigger this, even if that code is unused, because mpy_ld.py does not appear to strip dead code.

symptoms_visible: When I link my dynamic native module, mpy_ld.py exits with AssertionError: 11 for xtensawin and AssertionError: 2 for armv7emsp.
The failure appears when libm and libgcc object files needed by sinf/cosf are included, even if the calling code path is not used.
N0.label: N0 unsupported sin/cos relocations reported

symptoms_visible: After updating my project to the new linking support, the other ARM and Xtensawin builds are no longer a problem, but an armv6m module containing a floating-point division still stops in mpy_ld.py with AssertionError: 2.
The armv6m build fails with several GCC packages but succeeds with one Arch Linux GCC package.
N1.label: N1 archive linking adopted, armv6m case remains

symptoms_visible: Building the armv6m module with -fPIC instead of -fpic still reaches the same assertion for the absolute relocation.
N2.label: N2 fPIC probe unchanged

symptoms_visible: The minimal armv6m module still fails with my usual GCC packages, while the Arch Linux GCC build completes and produces the MPY file.
N3.label: N3 toolchain-dependent relocation output established

symptoms_visible: I have not yet retested my minimal armv6m example with a build containing the landed relocation change; my last own test still stopped at AssertionError: 2.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix landed, reporter verification pending

solution.intent: Adopt the newer native-module linking support that can load libgcc and libm archives and resolve their required object dependencies, then rebuild the module.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the newer mpy_ld.py linking support and pass the appropriate libgcc.a and libm.a archives to the linker instead of manually maintaining the extracted object list.

edges.comment: Reporter c41, following participant3 c40: the reporter updated emlearn-micropython to the new linking support. On the reporter's system it fixed almost everything, including the earlier ARM/Xtensawin cases, but exposed a remaining armv6m failure with a minimal floating-point division.

question_patterns: Could you rebuild the same minimal armv6m module with -fPIC instead of -fpic and report the linker output?
Does changing the position-independent-code compiler flag alter the armv6m failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried building the module with -fPIC, and it did not help. I still get caught on the same assertion due to the absolute relocation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With -fPIC the same armv6m module links and runs correctly, with no relocation assertion.
The traceback line number changes after updating MicroPython, but the build still stops on relocation type 2 with -fPIC.

edges.comment: Participant1 c46 requested the compiler-flag probe; reporter c47 ran it on the reporter's armv6m reproducer and reported the raw unchanged result. This is a handler-initiated build measurement, not a persistent fix.

question_patterns: Can you share the verbose output from the GCC package that successfully builds the same armv6m example?
What differs in the object and relocation output between a working and failing compiler package?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using the Arch Linux arm-none-eabi-gcc 14.2.0 package, the same command finishes and creates the MPY file. Its verbose output selects a different set and layout of libgcc objects; unlike my failing builds, it does not stop on relocation type 2. I pasted the complete successful build output for comparison.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The supposedly working Arch compiler produces the same relocation assertion when I rerun the minimal example.
A newer revision of the same Arch package also builds successfully and emits a slightly different list of helper objects.

edges.comment: Reporter c45 proactively supplied successful verbose output from the reporter's Arch Linux toolchain. The answer records only the observable build result and object selection; determining why the failing objects require unsupported text relocations is engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Extend mpy_ld.py's existing ARM absolute-relocation handling to R_ARM_ABS32 entries located in text sections, using the same relocation logic already used for read-only data, and ask the reporter to verify the landed change on the minimal armv6m module.
solution.concrete_example: Handle an R_ARM_ABS32 relocation in an ARM text section through the existing absolute-address relocation path used for read-only data. This covers cases where code loads an address from a literal or constant table embedded in text. Please rebuild the minimal armv6m division or sin/cos module with a current build and report whether it links and runs correctly.
solution.inference_hint: The final maintainer diagnosis in c50-c52 supersedes the earlier belief that runtime relocation tables or extensive opcode rewriting would be necessary. The failing case is an R_ARM_ABS32 relocation on data embedded in a text section, such as a constant-float table address loaded through a PC-relative ldr. Engineers determined that mpy_ld.py's existing read-only-data relocation logic could be reused for text sections.

edges.comment: Participant3 c50-c53: a maintainer implemented support, tested sin/cos on an armv6m RP2040, explained that the existing ro-data R_ARM_ABS32 logic also applies to text, and reported the change fixed. This is maintainer-side verification, not the reporter's own retest; therefore the terminal state remains unverified by the reporter.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: affected armv6m libgcc/libm objects contain R_ARM_ABS32 relocations for data or addresses embedded in text sections, while mpy_ld.py handled that absolute relocation in read-only data but not in text.
Must ground the diagnosis in the minimal floating-point-division failure, relocation type 2, the compiler-package-dependent object output, and the unchanged result with -fPIC.

The fix must route ARM text-section R_ARM_ABS32 entries through the existing absolute-relocation logic used for read-only data; it must not preserve the earlier claim that a new runtime relocation section or major opcode-rewriting system is necessarily required.
Must not present -fPIC as the solution, because the reporter tested it and observed the same assertion.

Must ask the reporter to rebuild and run the minimal armv6m division or sin/cos case on a build containing the fix before declaring the reporter's issue resolved; maintainer testing on an RP2040 does not substitute for the reporter's own verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Advanced embedded developer who builds MicroPython dynamic native modules, edits Makefiles, extracts objects from libgcc/libm archives, compares cross-compiler packages, and can inspect verbose linker and relocation output, but does not claim deep ELF relocation expertise.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and cooperative; supplies minimal reproducers and full build logs, distinguishes architectures and compiler versions carefully, and openly states uncertainty when interpreting relocations.
